item.title: Connected graphs with equal independence number and radius
item.description: arXiv:2610.30165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem states that the independence number of any connected graph is at least its radius. In 2007, DeLaVi\~na, Pepper, and Waller proved that every connected graph with equal independence number and radius is traceable. We first give a new short proof of this theorem and then prove two results for graphs of higher connectivity. (1) Every 2-connected graph with equal independence number and radius is Hamiltonian. (2) Every 3-connected graph with equal independence number and radius is Hamiltonian-connected and pancyclic. Several lemmas used in the proofs are of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Xingzhi Zhan

item.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.30166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Hillel Schein

item.title: An elementary proof of a tight $\Delta+1$ bound for the additive chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2610.30174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An additive coloring assigns positive integer labels to the vertices of a graph so that adjacent vertices have different sums of their neighbors' labels. The additive chromatic number $\eta(G)$ is the least $k$ for which labels from $[k]$ suffice. We give an elementary orientation argument proving that every finite simple graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G) \leq \Delta(G) + 1$. This argument yields a $(\Delta(G) + 1)$-additive-coloring in polynomial time and improves upon the current best bound of $\eta(G) \leq \Delta(G)^{2} - \Delta(G) + 1$, valid for $\Delta(G) \geq 2$, from Akbari, Ghanbari, Manaviyat, and Zare.
item.dc:creator: Alex Koutsoutis, Joseph Koutsoutis

item.title: Inverting Dependently Random Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2610.30185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\text{inv}(T)$ be the inversion index of the tournament $T$. Answering a question of Behague, we show that $\text{inv}(T_1\to T_2)=\text{inv}(T_1)+\text{inv}(T_2)$ does not even hold asymptotically.
item.dc:creator: Kada Williams

item.title: Syzygy and Adjoint Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.30283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.
item.dc:creator: Jaeho Shin

item.title: Cographs in chordal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $\gamma\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^\gamma$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.
item.dc:creator: Sepehr Hajebi

item.title: Permutation classes need not have proper growth rates
item.description: arXiv:2610.30369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By the Marcus-Tardos Theorem (formerly the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture), every permutation class other than the class of all permutations has a finite upper growth rate, meaning that the $n$th root of the number of permutations of length $n$ in the class has a finite limit superior. It has long been conjectured that this limit superior is in fact always a proper limit. We disprove this by constructing a permutation class whose upper and lower growth rates differ. The construction uses grid classes with cubic row-column graphs of increasing girth, obtained from Haar graphs of finite 2-groups. The corresponding hereditary property of ordered graphs also disproves an analogous 2006 conjecture of Balogh, Bollob\'as, and Morris. Along the way, we show that every proper permutation class with a D-finite generating function has a proper growth rate. We also establish refined enumerative bounds for grid classes, which lead to a short proof of Albert and Vatter's generalization of Bevan's Theorem on the growth rates of grid classes.
item.dc:creator: Jay Pantone, Vincent Vatter

item.title: Asymptotical results on the automorphism groups of canonical double cover of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The canonical double cover $BX$ of a graph $X$ is the direct product $X\times K_2$. A graph $X$ is stable if every automorphism of $BX$ is induced by automorphisms of $X$ and $K_2$, and unstable otherwise. We prove several asymptotic results on stable and unstable graphs. In particular, we show that the automorphism group of the canonical double cover of almost every graph has order $2$, and consequently that almost all graphs are stable. We also prove that the dominant sources of instability are having twins and being disconnected, in that order, and that graphs arising from a known construction are the next step in this hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Bart{\l}omiej Bychawski, Ademir Hujdurovi\'c, {\DJ}or{\dj}e Mitrovi\'c, Gabriel Verret

item.title: A remoteness formula for generalized Wythoff games
item.description: arXiv:2610.30427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smith's remoteness function records how long an impartial game lasts when the winner wins as quickly as possible and the loser delays defeat. For the generalized Wythoff game $\mathrm{WYT}(a,b)$, in which two positive integer parameters $a$ and $b$ determine which simultaneous removals from the two piles are allowed, we give a formula for the remoteness of every position, building on the known values at losing positions. The formula depends on two indices: a local index determined by the coordinates of the losing positions in a window of length $b$ ending at the smaller pile, and the integer part of the pile difference divided by $a$. When $b=1$, complementary Beatty sequences make the local index explicit, which gives an explicit formula for $\mathrm{WYT}(a,1)$, including classical Wythoff's game. We also show that if each attempted move in a finite impartial game independently fails with a fixed probability and passes the turn, the probability that the player to move wins under optimal play is an explicit exponential function of remoteness. For every success probability strictly between $0$ and $1$, the optimal attempts are exactly the moves that reduce remoteness by one.
item.dc:creator: Ra\'ul S\'anchez Gal\'an, Yijie Xu

item.title: Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Giulio Cerbai, Anders Claesson

item.title: A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.
item.dc:creator: Zhentao Li

item.title: The linearity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Linearity Conjecture states that in the projective plane PG(2,$q$), $q=p^h$, every minimal blocking set (w.r.t. lines) is a linear point set over some subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$. This paper contains the proof of the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\ne 3,4$, where $e$ is the exponent of the blocking set. The text contains 3 concatenated parts. In Part 0, we give a guide for reading Parts 1 and 2. Part 1 develops a great part of the method, and the case $p^e=2$ is solved. In Part 2 we prove the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Peter Sziklai

item.title: Asymptotically Sharp Length Thresholds for \texorpdfstring{$q$}{q}-ary Codes with Distances \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2} and \texorpdfstring{$4$}{4}
item.description: arXiv:2610.30613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $q\ge5$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of a $q$-ary Hamming space of length $n$ in which every two distinct words have distance $2$ or $4$. Set \[ N(q)=\left\lceil\max\left\{2q+1, \frac{17+\sqrt{8q^2+96q-95}}2\right\}\right\rceil. \] We prove that $A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2$ for every $n\ge N(q)$. In particular, $N(q)=2q+1$ for $q\ge26$. An explicit code of size $q(n-2)$ shows that the least eventual threshold $N_*(q)$ satisfies $N_*(q)\ge2q-1$; consequently $2q-1\le N_*(q)\le2q+1$ for every $q\ge26$. The argument applies to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, without a linearity assumption. Its main ingredients are synchronization of symbols on intersecting supports, weighted bounds for $2$-intersecting families of four-sets, and a joint estimate for the weight-two and weight-four layers in a common-three-core configuration. No computational verification is required.
item.dc:creator: Valjakas Djaljapayan, Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Wei-Hsuan Yu

item.title: The Ternary and Quaternary Cases of the $\{2,4\}$-Distance Code Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $q\ge2$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of an unrestricted $q$-ary code of length $n$ in which any two distinct words have Hamming distance $2$ or $4$. We prove that \[ A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2 \qquad(q\in\{3,4\},\ n\ge6), \] thereby settling the two remaining alphabet sizes in the conjecture of Boyvalenkov, Delchev, Zinoviev, and Zinoviev; the binary case was settled previously. The quaternary result implies the ternary result by alphabet inclusion. For $n\ge16$, the quaternary upper bound is proved combinatorially. After normalizing one word to zero, the weight-four supports form a $2$-intersecting family; exact support intersections force symbol synchronization and restrict support multiplicities. We combine the nontrivial intersection theorem with matching arguments and a three-coordinate projection lemma. The finite lengths $6\le n\le13$ are handled by a complete Hamming-isometry reduction to exact clique decisions, and $n=14,15$ by a smaller exact weighted-clique relaxation. All finite decisions are reproduced by two standalone integer-only C++17 verifiers provided as supplementary source files.
item.dc:creator: Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Valjakas Djaljapayan, Wei-Hsuan Yu

item.title: NP-Hardness of Generalized-Tur\'an Graph Modification Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For graphs $G, T$ and a graph-family $\mathcal{H}$, let $ex(G,T,\mathcal{H})$ denote the maximum possible number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{H}$-free subgraph of $G$. Alon and Shikhelman conjectured that for every family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$ with $\chi(H) > s$ for every $H \in \mathcal{H}$, it is NP-hard to compute $ex(G,K_s,\mathcal{H})$, and even to approximate it up to additive error $n^{s-\delta}$ on $n$-vertex graphs, for any fixed $\delta > 0$. The case $s=2$ was established in a breakthrough result of Alon, Shapira and Sudakov. We prove the Alon-Shikhelman conjecture for finite families $\mathcal{H}$. In particular, we obtain an elementary proof of the Alon-Shapira-Sudakov result when $\mathcal{H}$ is finite.
item.dc:creator: Lior Gishboliner, Yevgeny Levanzov, Asaf Shapira

item.title: Aleshin graphs are expanders
item.description: arXiv:2610.30662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Aleshin level graphs are two-sided expanders. We establish linear diameter bounds for Belaterra and Aleshin graph families. At level $n$, the diameters of the Bellaterra and undirected Aleshin graphs are a $|V_n|=2^n$. This improves the quadratic diameter bounds of Malyshev and Pak to the correct order of growth. For the Aleshin graphs we obtain a normalized spectral gap of at least $1-2\sqrt2/3$ and an edge-expansion constant of at least $3-2\sqrt2$, thereby establishing a Malyshev--Pak's Conjecture with explicit constants. An exact calculation at level ten also proves that the undirected Aleshin graphs are not Ramanujan for any $n\geq10$.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharlampovich, Alina Vdovina

item.title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.
item.dc:creator: Jiyou Li, Sicheng Zhao

item.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.30712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Samuel J. Ferguson, Joshua Iosevich

item.title: Weighted odd-cycle transversals and fractional colorings of planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We bound fractional chromatic numbers by establishing a connection with low-weight odd-cycle transversals. Let $\ell\geq 3$ be an integer and let $G$ be a graph of odd girth at least $\ell$ whose odd-cycle covering polyhedron is integral. For every nonnegative weight vector $w=(w_v)_{v\in V(G)}\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{V(G)}$, we obtain a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G-Z$ is bipartite and $w(Z)\leq\frac{mad(G)}{2\ell}w(V(G))$. Here, $w(S)=\sum_{v\in S}w_v$ for any $S\subseteq V(G)$, and $mad(G)$ denotes the maximum average degree of $G$. Consequently, if $mad(G)<2\ell$, then $G$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{4\ell}{2\ell-mad(G)}$. As applications, we prove that, for every positive integer $k$, every $n$-vertex planar graph of girth at least $2k+3$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{2k+1}{k}(1-\frac{1}{kn+1})$, establishing the girth version of Naserasr's fractional coloring conjecture with a strict inequality. For $k=1$, we furthermore prove that the upper bound $\frac{3n}{n+1}$ holds for every $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph and this is attained for infinitely many values of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolan Hu, Jiaao Li, Zhouningxin Wang

item.title: Probabilistic and game thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.30730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a finite set and $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^X$ a non-trivial increasing property. We show that the bias-threshold $b(\mathcal{F})$ for the Picker-Chooser $\mathcal{F}$-game satisfies $b(\mathcal{F}) \ge \alpha / p_c(\mathcal{F})$, where $p_c(\mathcal{F})$ is the threshold for the property $\mathcal{F}$ and $\alpha > 0$ is an absolute constant. This proves that Picker-Chooser games satisfy one-sided ``probabilistic intuition''. The proof is based on the notion of influence from the theory of boolean functions.
item.dc:creator: Rajko Nenadov

item.title: Arithmetic Conditions for the Invertibility of Circulant Matrices over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.30830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates arithmetic conditions, over finite fields, for the invertibility of circulant matrices whose first row is $(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$, in terms of linear constraints on the entries $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}$. The coefficients of such linear constraints are determined by field traces arising from Frobenius orbits of roots of unity, and under additional assumptions they are given by Ramanujan sums reduced modulo the characteristic of the given field. These results provide finite-field analogues of the corresponding criteria over $\mathbb{Q}$, where the relevant Ramanujan-sum linear constraints can be formulated without such additional assumptions, while also showing some differences caused by reduction modulo the characteristic. The constraints can often determine invertibility using aggregate information about the entries of a row, rather than the particular pattern of the entries. We also discuss the polynomial gcd criterion, which gives necessary and sufficient conditions for invertibility and yields further consequences for special families of circulant matrices.
item.dc:creator: Jeong-Ok Choi, Youngmi Hur

item.title: The signless Laplacian spectral Tur\'{a}n problems for disjoint triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.30859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Tur\'{a}n-type problem for graphs forbidding $k$ disjoint triangles has been resolved firstly by Erd\H{o}s [Arch. Math. 13 (1962) 222-227] for graphs of sufficiently large order and improved by Moon [Canad. J. Math. 20 (1968) 95-102], who established that the unique edge extremal graph is $K_{k-1}\vee T_2(n-k+1)$ for $n> \frac{19k-11}{2}$. In this paper, we determine the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $kK_3$-free graphs of order $n$ and characterize the unique signless Laplacian spectral extremal graph $K_{k-1}\vee T_{2}(n-k+1)$ for all $k\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Zhu Chen, Ya-Lei Jin, Peng-Li Zhang

item.title: On the maximal index of $C_4^-$-free unbalanced signed graphs of prescribed size
item.description: arXiv:2610.30881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The extremal problem of determining the graphs with maximum spectral radius among all graphs with a prescribed number of edges was resolved by Rowlinson [Linear Algebra Appl. 110 (1988) 43--53]. A signed graph $\Gamma=(G,\sigma)$ is called $C_k^-$-free if it contains no negative $k$-cycle as a signed subgraph. The index of a signed graph is defined as the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. This paper addresses the maximization of the index of unbalanced signed graphs. For signed graphs of a prescribed order, Wang and Lin [Discrete Appl. Math. 372 (2025) 164--172] determined the maximum index of $C_4^{-}$-free unbalanced signed graphs. Subsequently, Wang, Peng and Hou [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114871] characterized the unbalanced signed graphs of prescribed size with maximum index. This paper treats the edge spectral Tur\'an-type problem for $C_4^-$-free unbalanced signed graphs. The all-positive signed graph with underlying graph $G$ is denoted by $(G,+)$. Evidently, $A((G,+))=A(G)$. In particular, $(H_{d,t},+)$ is the all-positive signed graph whose underlying graph is $H_{d,t}$, where $H_{d,0}=K_d$ and for $t>0$, $H_{d,t}$ is obtained from $K_d$ by adding a single vertex adjacent to exactly $t$ vertices of $K_d$. Let $m-3=\binom{d}{2}+t$ with $0\le t\le d-1$. Up to switching isomorphism and the addition of isolated vertices, the unique extremal unbalanced signed graph is obtained by attaching a negative triangle to a specified vertex of the all-positive signed graph $(H_{d,t},+)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhihui Yang, Dan Li, Yuanyuan Chen

item.title: Spectral and edge conditions for negative Hamiltonian cycles in unbalanced signed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral conditions for Hamiltonian cycles are a fundamental subject in extremal spectral graph theory. For simple unsigned graphs, Fiedler and Nikiforov [Linear Algebra Appl., 432 (2010), 2170-2173] pioneered this direction, and Li and Ning [Linear Multilinear Algebra, 64 (2016), 2252-2269] later extended these results by introducing minimum degree parameters. In this paper, we study the spectral conditions for the existence of a negative Hamiltonian cycle in unbalanced signed graphs of order n > 8. We first determine the maximum index among all n-vertex unbalanced signed graphs containing no negative Hamiltonian cycle, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs up to switching isomorphism. Furthermore, we establish an upper bound on the number of edges in unbalanced signed graphs of order n >= 7 with frustration index one, and classify all extremal graphs achieving this bound.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Zha

item.title: Two refined Wilf-equivalences for patterns of length 4 and a conjecture on Dumont permutations of the first kind
item.description: arXiv:2610.30975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a bijection between $2143$-avoiding and $3421$-avoiding permutations that preserves the descent top set and the ascent top set and reverses the left-to-right order of the peaks. This bijection allows us to establish a bijection between $1243$-avoiding and $3412$-avoiding permutations with the same properties. These results refine two cases of a conjecture posed by Burstein and prove a conjecture posed by Burstein and Jones.
item.dc:creator: Zuo-Ru Zhang, Hongkuan Zhao

item.title: Nonexistence of Constant Congruences for the Cumulative Partition Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.31102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p(n)$ be the ordinary partition function and let $c(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(k)$, with $c(0)=0$. We prove that, for every $a\geq1$, $b\geq0$, and $m\geq2$, the sequence $c(an+b)$ is not eventually constant modulo $m$, thereby answering a question posed by Chen. The proof combines the algebraicity over $\mathbb C(j)$ of modular functions for finite-index subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ with Voloch's theorem on the transcendence of elliptic modular functions in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Kathy Q. Ji

item.title: Zero Forcing, Support Varieties, and Boundary Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let a finite simple graph be given. We study symmetric matrices with this graph pattern that admit a null vector with prescribed exact support. Such a vector exists precisely when its support is a fort, meaning that no vertex outside the support has exactly one neighbor inside it. Over the complex numbers, we prove that the Zariski closure of each exact-support coefficient locus is irreducible and compute its codimension in terms of boundary vertices and a labeled forest on the connected components of the support. The corresponding forest deficiency also determines the generic restricted nullity. An incidence parametrization yields a prime decomposition of the reduced zero-forcing failure locus. For a prescribed common kernel, we describe the coefficient space through equilibrium stresses, exterior affine dependencies, and free coefficients. We then construct boundary complexes recording local solution values and equation residuals. Their gluing maps are defined over the universal coefficient ring and commute with arbitrary base change. By retaining the complete collection of support signatures associated with each seed set, we obtain a composition formula for the minimum zero-forcing number and an algorithm for its computation.
item.dc:creator: Zongjian Han, Yiran Liang

item.title: Zero Forcing on Maximal Outerplanar Graphs: Capacities and Phase Repair
item.description: arXiv:2610.31138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the zero-forcing number of maximal biconnected outerplanar graphs. When the weak dual is a path, the zero-forcing number and the induced path-covering number are both two. Otherwise, the branching faces determine a canonical core and a family of terminal strips. We prove that an optimal forcing process can be chosen in a normal form governed by explicit vertex and face capacities on the core. After fixing forests on the terminal strips, the zero-forcing number is expressed through an optimization over core-edge selections and the minimum number of root connections that must be removed to obtain an executable orientation. The path-covering number is obtained from the same capacity optimization without the repair cost. We characterize executable orientations by blocking-circuit equations and identify the two-path obstruction with a first cohomology class of a signed contact multigraph. Local replacements and a finite comparison of boundary recurrences establish the normal form for graphs of arbitrary size. A fifty-six-state recurrence constructs a minimum zero-forcing set and a complete forcing chronology in linear time from indexed triangle adjacency. We also obtain exact replacement results for rooted blocks and construct infinite families in which the zero-forcing number exceeds the path-covering number.
item.dc:creator: Zongjian Han, Yiran Liang

item.title: An algebraic proof of 1-extension
item.description: arXiv:2610.31212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new proof that 1-extension preserves generic local rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in all dimensions. The proof does not use a special position argument, which makes the approach potentially useful for X-replacement in 3-space. Instead, the balancing conditions recently introduced by the first author use directed paths in the line graph, and by modifying the end of these paths, we transfer a self-stress on the 1-extended graph back to the original. Treating the new vertex as variable allows us to extract the balancing condition of the smaller graph as one coefficient of a homogeneous quadratic. A Lean 4 formalization of the main results accompanies the paper.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Heaton, Martin Winter

item.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: $S(6)\ge 537$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000). Known recursive constructions then give the improved lower bounds $S(8)\ge 5\,372$, $S(11)\ge 204\,208$, $S(13)\ge 2\,042\,082$, and $R_6(3)\ge 539$. We also report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions found by the search. We describe their structure and provide the complete partitions in the supplementary material. These partitions provide starting points for future searches and structural studies of Schur partitions.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyang Chen, Ligeng Zhu, Fan Long

item.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.31475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.
item.dc:creator: William F. Klostermeyer

item.title: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies
item.description: arXiv:2610.31499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $\omega:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,\omega)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$. Gollin et al.[1] proved, using the Axiom of Choice, that a finite optimal strategy exists for every finite graph, every nonnegative initial weight function and every target vertex; see Tao [2] for a simplified proof. We prove that the lengths of shortest optimal strategies on $3$-spiders have no uniform finite bound. In particular, these lengths cannot be bounded in terms of the maximum degree of the graph.
item.dc:creator: Guanheng Chen, Ran Tao, Tianyi Tao

item.title: Functions determining $(q+3)/2$ directions over the finite field with $q$ elements
item.description: arXiv:2610.31516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q=p^n$, where $p>2$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-set $U\subseteq\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ determining exactly $(q+3)/2$ directions is affinely equivalent to the graph of $x^{(q+1)/2}$. For $n\ge2$, we also prove that a $q$-set determining at most $(q+p)/2$ directions is either an affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear set or affinely equivalent to this graph. The classification for $n=1$ is due to Lov\'asz and Schrijver. For $n=2$, the classification and the stated stability result follow from results of G\'acs, Lov\'asz, and Sz\H onyi and the direction theorems of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme, and Sz\H onyi, completed by Ball. These direction theorems establish affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linearity for functions with fewer than $(q+3)/2$ determined directions. Our proof uses R\'edei polynomials, results of G\'acs, Lov\'asz, and Sz\H onyi on their coefficients, and an earlier polynomial comparison lemma of the author.
item.dc:creator: Bence Csajb\'ok

item.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
item.description: arXiv:2610.31533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: The domination number of the 2-token graph of the complete bipartite graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.31557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, the $2$-token graph $F_2(G)$ has as vertices all $2$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two such subsets adjacent whenever their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper, we determine the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, for all integers $2\le m\le n$. We show that it equals $\lceil m/2\rceil+n-1$, except when $m=3$, or when $m\ge5$ is odd and $n=m+1$; in these two exceptional situations it is one less. Our arguments rely on an explicit characterization of the dominating sets of the $2$-token graph of $K_{m,n}$.
item.dc:creator: E. Acosta Troncoso, I. Caldera Caldera, L. M. Rivera

item.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel G\'abor Simon

item.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
item.description: arXiv:2610.31602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.
item.dc:creator: Mikey Becht, Darij Grinberg

item.title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.31607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.
item.dc:creator: Vassily Gorbounov, Christian Korff, Leonardo C. Mihalcea

item.title: The Asymptotic Number of Anticodes in Hamming Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Hamming space $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, a $d$-anticode is a subset in which every pair of points has Hamming distance at most $d$, or equivalently, a set of diameter at most $d$. Let $m_q(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of a $d$-anticode and let $\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)$ be the family of all $d$-anticodes. We show that for fixed $q$, as $n\to\infty$, the total number of $d$-anticodes satisfies \[ |\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)|=2^{(1+o(1))m_q(n,d)} \] for $4\le d\le n-1$, except when $q=2$ and $d=n-1$. We also count linear $d$-anticodes, that is, subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ with diameter at most $d$. For fixed $q$ and $d$, their number is polynomial in $n$. For growing $d$, we determine the exponential order as $q^{\Theta_q(d^2+d\log_q(n/d))}$ in the sublinear regime and $q^{\Theta(n^2)}$ when $d/n\to\alpha\in(0,1)$. In the near-full regime $n-d=o(n)$, we obtain the sharper count $q^{(1/4+o(1))n^2}$. A random-generator construction further improves the binary lower bound for every fixed linear diameter.
item.dc:creator: Anna-Lena Horlemann, Ananthakrishnan Ravi

item.title: Strongly Regular Graph Construction via Quadratic Binary Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.30142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Strongly regular graphs, hereafter SRGs, are highly structured combinatorial objects of central interest in algebraic graph theory and quantum information, whose explicit construction becomes rapidly intractable as the number of vertices grows; Conway's still unresolved $99$-graph problem is an emblematic example. The matrix equation defining SRGs is quadratic in the binary edge variables, so the natural penalty enforcing it, a sum of squared residuals, is quartic and lies outside quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, known as QUBO. We prove a considerably stronger obstruction, namely that no quadratic function of the edge variables has the labeled SRGs as its exact set of global minimizers, except for three degenerate families given by the perfect matchings, the cocktail-party graphs and the pentagon. In particular, we formally establish that the $99$-vertex graph of Conway's problem cannot be obtained from any QUBO over the edge variables without auxiliary variables. Guided by this theorem we develop two complementary algorithms. The first operates within pure QUBO, solves the degenerate families exactly, and beyond them works as a generate--prune--verify pipeline whose output is a reduced set of candidates certified by a polynomial-time classical test. The second solves the full problem by quadratizing this quartic penalty through Rosenberg auxiliary variables, whose number grows as $\Theta(N^3)$ with the number of vertices $N$. We test the pure-QUBO route under simulated annealing on all feasible families with at most $18$ vertices and the auxiliary-variable route on representative targets up to $16$ vertices, and tabulate the algebraically feasible parameter sets for graphs with at most $49$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: D. Osorio, P. Andagana, V. Gonz\'alez, J. Czartowski, D. Goyeneche

item.title: Combinatorial formulas for the multivariate Markov-Krein transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.30155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we study the Markov--Krein correspondence in both the univariate and multivariate settings. Our main result provides an explicit moment--moment formula expressing the multivariate moments of the inverse Markov--Krein transform in terms of the multivariate moments of the Markov-Krein transform via cyclic interval partitions. We also derive moment--cumulant relations involving classical, Boolean and free cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Julian Zazueta-Obeso

item.title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $\alpha$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ \omega_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq \alpha^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^k\omega_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $\omega\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.
item.dc:creator: Guo-Dong Hong

item.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.30382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Victor Dubach

item.title: Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest for $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $\alpha$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $\beta$. For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{\alpha,\beta}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way. On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $\Omega(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(\alpha,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $\alpha>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded. Finally, for every fixed rationals $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,\alpha,\beta)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025]. [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]
item.dc:creator: Li-Hsuan Chen, Florent Foucaud, Ling-Ju Hung, Ralf Klasing, Lucas Lorieau, Peter Rossmanith

item.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.30711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]
item.dc:creator: Yuan Si

item.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: On the generation of the symmetric group by index relations of three prefix reversals
item.description: arXiv:2610.30892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The cubic pancake graphs are Cayley graphs over the symmetric group Sn generated by three prefix reversals. There is the folllowing open problem: characterize all the sets of three prefix reversals that generate Sn. Blanco and Golubyatnikov give a complete solution of the problem when any of the two smallest or the two largest lengths but n are included in a triple of prefix reversals. According to their conjectures, we give some conditions implying a triple of prefix reversals does not generate Sn. Moreover, Using the symmetric groups that can already be generated by three prefix reversals, we can derive some recurrence conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yexiao Lei, Jinxing Zhao, Ziyu Zhu, Yang Wu

item.title: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langle\sigma_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langle\sigma_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix. Using this, we define sum-rank Reed--Muller-type codes and show that their dimension and minimum distance are given by the formulas for affine Cartesian codes with side lengths $\mathrm{deg}\,H_1,\ldots,\mathrm{deg}\,H_m$; the same holds for codes supported on lower sets. The family contains as special cases linearized Reed--Solomon codes, Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed--Muller codes, and affine Cartesian codes. Over finite fields, every linearized Reed--Muller code of Berardini and Caruso is, after a monomial change of variables, a monomial code in our framework. This gives the dimension of all these codes, and their exact minimum distance in every degree whenever the support is a lower set.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Neri, Giuseppe Zampella

item.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.31460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range. At $m=4$ and $m=6$, the only exceptions are, respectively, the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families; these occur only in dimension two over fields of characteristic two. For arbitrary $m\geqslant3$, we also establish two uniform bounds. If $\sqrt q\geqslant12(m+1)\log(2m+2)$, no word of interpolation degree $k+m$ is a deep hole when $q$ is odd, $k\geqslant3$, or $m$ is odd. If $q>16(m+2)^4$, we obtain the corresponding complete classification at every admissible $k$, including the explicit dimension-two exceptions. Our proofs use an agreement criterion expressed in complete homogeneous symmetric functions, agreement-count estimates, finite geometry, permutation-polynomial restrictions, and subset constructions for solving the resulting symmetric-function equations. The remaining finite cases are settled by finite computations with supplied certificates and deterministic verification programs.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Fan

item.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
item.description: arXiv:2610.31513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.
item.dc:creator: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

item.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{\Delta/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $\Delta \geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In contrast, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Basak, Shaibal Karmakar

item.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
item.description: arXiv:2610.31638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Does computing a composition of total Boolean functions require the product of the randomized query complexities of its factors? We give a negative answer. There are families of total functions $f,g$ such that $R(f\circ g) =\Theta\!\left(\frac1{\log R(g)}\right)R(f)R(g)$ This result requires first separating linearized query complexity $\LR$, as well as noisy randomized query complexity $noisyR$, from standard randomized query complexity $R$. Both constructions essentially come from totalizing existing partial function separations, albeit via different techniques. By adapting these techniques, we also construct total functions separating every adjacent pair in the chain from sabotage $RS$, max-conflict $\bar{\chi}$, and linearised query complexity $LR$. We show that AND-of-ORs separates conflict $\chi$ from max-conflict $\bar{\chi}$ complexity and makes conflict and sabotage incomparable. Finally, randomized complexity can be smaller than its composition limit $R^*$ by the maximal factor $\Theta(\log R)$. The total--total composition separation is also formalized in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Meiburg

item.title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
item.description: arXiv:2205.05125v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Reading, Salvatore Stella

item.title: Locked Polyomino Tilings
item.description: arXiv:2307.15996v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A locked $t$-omino tiling is a grid tiling by $t$-ominoes such that, if you remove any pair of tiles, the only way to fill in the remaining $2t$ grid cells with $t$-ominoes is to use the same two tiles in the exact same configuration as before. We exclude degenerate cases where there is only one tiling overall due to small dimensions. It is a classic (and straightforward) result that finite grids do not admit locked 2-omino tilings. In this paper, we construct explicit locked $t$-omino tilings for $t\geq3$ on square and rectangular grids of various dimensions. We show that locked 3- and 4-omino tilings exist on finite square grids of arbitrarily large size. The result for 4-omino tilings in particular is remarkable because they are so rare and difficult to construct: Only a single tiling is known to exist on any grid up to size $40\times40$. We also find locked 5- and 6-omino tilings, and provide a computer-assisted proof that locked 7-omino tilings do not exist on any rectangular grid. In a weighted version of the problem where vertices of the grid may have weights from the set $\{1,2\}$ that count toward the total tile size, we demonstrate the existence of locked tilings on arbitrarily large square weighted grids with only 6 tiles. Finally, we construct locked $t$-omino tilings of the infinite grid for arbitrarily large $t$. Locked $t$-omino tilings arise as obstructions to widely used political redistricting algorithms in a model of redistricting where the underlying census geography is a grid graph. Most prominent is the ReCom Markov chain, which takes a random walk on the space of redistricting plans by iteratively merging and splitting pairs of districts (tiles) at a time. Locked $t$-omino tilings are isolated states in the state space of ReCom. The constructions in this paper are counterexamples to the meta-conjecture that ReCom is irreducible on graphs of practical interest.
item.dc:creator: Jamie Tucker-Foltz

item.title: String attractors and bi-infinite words
item.description: arXiv:2403.13449v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: String attractors are a combinatorial tool coming from the field of data compression. It is a set of positions within a word which captures an occurrence of every factor. While one-sided infinite words admitting a finite string attractor are eventually periodic, the situation is different for two-sided infinite words. In this article, we characterise the bi-infinite words admitting a finite string attractor as the eventually periodic words, the characteristic Sturmian words and their morphic images. For words that do not admit finite string attractors, we study the structure and properties of their infinite string attractors.
item.dc:creator: Pierre B\'eaur, France Gheeraert, Benjamin Hellouin de Menibus

item.title: Approximating Kemeny's constant via spectral sparsification
item.description: arXiv:2503.13382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kemeny's constant of a network quantifies the expected time for a random walk to reach a target vertex chosen according to the stationary distribution, independently of the starting vertex. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, we introduce the class of slightly regular networks, whose orthogonal degree vector is an eigenvector of the Laplacian, and derive an exact expression for Kemeny's constant for this class, extending previous results beyond regular networks. Second, we address the efficient approximation of Kemeny's constant using spectral sparsification. We establish multiplicative bounds relating Kemeny's constant of a network to that of any of its spectral sparsifiers, and use these bounds to design an approximation algorithm. While standard exact approaches based on a full spectral decomposition or on the computation of a pseudoinverse have $O(n^3)$ complexity, our method has complexity $O(n^2\log^{1+o(1)}n)$ for fixed approximation parameters, and is therefore nearly quadratic in the number of vertices even for dense networks.
item.dc:creator: Aida Abiad, \'Angeles Carmona, Andr\'es M. Encinas, Maria Jos\'e Jim\'enez, \'Alvaro Samperio

item.title: Singular walks in the quarter plane and Bernoulli numbers
item.description: arXiv:2504.13542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider singular (aka genus $0$) walks in the quarter plane and their associated generating functions $Q(x,y,t)$, which enumerate the walks starting from the origin, of fixed endpoint (encoded by the spatial variables $x$ and $y$) and of fixed length (encoded by the time variable $t$). We first prove that the previous series can be extended up to a universal value of $t$ (in the sense that this holds for all singular models), namely $t=\frac{1}{2}$, and we provide a probabilistic interpretation of $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$. As a second step, we refine earlier results in the literature and show that $Q(x,y,t)$ is indeed differentially transcendental for any $t\in(0,\frac{1}{2}]$. Moreover, we prove that $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$ is strongly differentially transcendental. As a last step, we show that for certain models the series expansion of $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$ is directly related to Bernoulli numbers. This provides a second proof of its strong differential transcendence.
item.dc:creator: Alin Bostan, Lucia Di Vizio, Kilian Raschel

item.title: An Intersection Product for the Polytope Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2504.16678v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new multiplication for the polytope algebra, defined via the intersection of polytopes. After establishing the foundational properties of this intersection product, we investigate finite-dimensional subalgebras that arise naturally from this construction. These subalgebras can be regarded as volumetric analogues of the graded M\"obius algebra, which appears in the context of the Dowling--Wilson conjecture. We conjecture that they also satisfy the injective hard Lefschetz property and the Hodge--Riemann relations, and we prove these in degree one.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Wannerer

item.title: The Sch\"utzenberger involution and colored lattice models
item.description: arXiv:2505.07806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ. In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously. For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Sch\"utzenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.
item.dc:creator: Henrik P. A. Gustafsson, Carl Westerlund

item.title: Inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of matroids under deletion
item.description: arXiv:2510.01086v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a deletion formula for the inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial and the inverse $Z$-polynomial of a matroid. Our formulas provide analogues to the deletion formulas of Braden--Vysogorets for Kazhdan--Lusztig and $Z$-polynomials. We discuss several consequences, which include closed formulas and recursions for these invariants on uniform matroids, projective geometries, glued cycles, and arbitrary matroids of corank $2$. As a relevant application of our deletion formula, we show the existence of a matroid of rank $19$ which disproves a conjecture of Xie and Zhang concerning a real-rootedness property of inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Tom Braden, Luis Ferroni, Jacob P. Matherne, Nutan Nepal

item.title: A modern perspective on Tutte's homotopy theorem
item.description: arXiv:2601.02582v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We begin with a review of Tutte's homotopy theory, which concerns the structure of a certain graph associated to a matroid (together with some extra data). Concretely, Tutte's path theorem asserts that this graph is connected, and his homotopy theorem asserts that every cycle in the graph is a composition of ``elementary cycles'', which come in four different flavors. We present an extended version of the homotopy theorem, in which we give a more refined classification of the different types of elementary cycles. We explain in detail how the path theorem allows one to prove that the foundation of a matroid (in the sense of Baker--Lorscheid) is generated by universal cross-ratios, and how the extended homotopy theorem allows one to classify all algebraic relations between universal cross-ratios. The resulting ``fundamental presentation'' of the foundation was previously established in [Baker--Lorscheid], but the argument here is more self-contained. We then recall a few applications of the fundamental presentation to the representation theory of matroids. Finally, in the most novel but also the most speculative part of the paper, we discuss what a ``higher Tutte homotopy theorem'' might look like, and we present some preliminary computations along these lines. The appendices include modern language translations of Tutte's proofs of the path theorem and the homotopy theorem (the latter is a contribution by Ju\v{s} Kocutar).
item.dc:creator: Matthew Baker, Tong Jin, Oliver Lorscheid

item.title: New upper bounds for the period of a negative orientable sequence
item.description: arXiv:2602.04433v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Negative orientable sequences, i.e. periodic sequences with elements from a finite alphabet of size at least three in which an n-tuple or the negative of its reverse appears at most once in a period of the sequence, were introduced by Alhakim et al. in 2024. The main goal in defining them was as a means of generating orientable sequences, which have automatic position location applications, although they are potentially of interest in their own right. In this paper we develop new upper bounds on the period of negative orientable sequences which, for n>2, are significantly sharper than the previous known bound. The approach used to develop the new bounds involves examining the nodes in the subgraph of the de Bruijn graph corresponding to a negative orientable sequence, and to consider the implications of the fact that the in-degree of every vertex in this subgraph must equal the out-degree. However, despite improving the bounds, a gap remains between the largest known period for a negative orientable sequence and the corresponding bounds for every n>2.
item.dc:creator: Chris J Mitchell, Peter R Wild

item.title: A Recognizable Substitution for the Anti-Penrose Tiling
item.description: arXiv:2603.15549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a substitution on six marked rhombs, called Seabed, with inflation factor $\varphi^3$. We prove that its tiling space is mutually locally derivable with the unmarked Anti-Penrose pentagrid hull. Eleven vertex patches of depth at most four recognize the parent vertices: their acceptance domains coincide with the five internally contracted windows. Matching the fine tiles around each parent rhomb to a replacement patch recovers their markings uniquely. The inverse local maps have a uniform finite radius and extend to all singular limit tilings in the hull. The construction also gives a recognizable parent hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Miki Imura

item.title: Signless Laplacian spectral radius of simplicial complexes without $r$-dimensional wheels
item.description: arXiv:2604.04536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An $r$-dimensional wheel is defined as the join of an $(r-2)$-simplex and a cycle. In this paper, we study the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of $n$-vertex $r$-dimensional pure simplicial complexes that contain no $r$-dimensional wheels. For sufficiently large $n$, we determine the extremal complexes that attain this maximum. Our result generalizes the corresponding extremal results of signless Laplacian on graphs and provides a spectral anlogue of a theorem of Brown, Erd\H{o}s and S\'os on the maximum number of facets of simplicial complexes in the case $r=2$.
item.dc:creator: Huan-Zhi Zhang, Yi-Zheng Fan

item.title: On $4$-perfect-matching covers of cubic graphs with two adjacent odd circuits in a $2$-factor
item.description: arXiv:2605.09475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a cubic graph admitting a $2$-factor consisting of exactly two odd circuits, and let the complementary $1$-factor contain precisely three spokes (along with an arbitrary number of chords). We show that four perfect matchings can cover $G$. As a consequence, $G$ fulfils the $7/5$-Conjecture of Alon and Tarsi.
item.dc:creator: J\'an Karab\'a\v{s}, Edita M\'a\v{c}ajov\'a

item.title: Schur positivity of the nabla operator on two-column modified Hall--Littlewood polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2605.20954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler (1999) introduced two Schur positivity conjectures concerning the action of the $\nabla$ operator on modified Hall--Littlewood polynomials. Although the proofs of the celebrated compositional shuffle conjecture and its rational generalization, along with various symmetric function identities, have largely resolved these conjectures in the affirmative, we provide an elegant alternative proof driven by $q$-series techniques. Through this approach, we derive explicit Schur function expansions for two-column partitions and extend our results to arbitrary positive powers $\nabla^k$.
item.dc:creator: Menghao Qu

item.title: On the Realizability of Edge-Girth Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2607.25629v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The edge-girth of an edge $e$ in a simple connected graph is the length of a shortest cycle containing $e$, with $g_e = \infty$ if no such cycle exists, and the edge-girth sequence of a graph is the nondecreasing sequence of the edge-girths of its edges. We characterize the sequences that are realizable as the edge-girth sequence of a simple connected graph. A constant sequence $(g^{(m)})$ with $g$ finite and $m \geq 1$ is realizable if and only if $m = g$ or $m \geq \lceil 3g/2 \rceil$. Otherwise, writing $S = S_0 \uplus (g^{(m)})$, where $g$ is the maximum value of $S$ and $m$ its multiplicity, we prove that $S$ is realizable if and only if $S_0$ is realizable and $m$ lies in an explicit set determined by $g$ and by the maximum diameters of the graphs realizing $S_0$, alone or extended by fewer than $g$ edges of edge-girth $g$. The proof rests on a chaining lemma, which turns a shortest cycle of a realization into a lower bound on the maximum diameter of the realizations of a shorter sequence.
item.dc:creator: Lilian Marey, Paul Hilaire, Charlotte Laclau

item.title: A proof of the 3-Decomposition Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.25385v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the 3-Decomposition Conjecture: every finite connected cubic loopless multigraph decomposes into a spanning tree, a 2-regular subgraph, and a matching. The proof rests on a new theorem on matching complements in subcubic graphs. Let H be a finite connected bridgeless simple graph of maximum degree three, and let S be its set of degree-two vertices, with |S| = k >= 2. We show that H has a matching of size equal to its cyclomatic number, |E(H)| - |V(H)| + 1, whose deletion leaves a single tree containing all of S, together with cycles disjoint from S. The proof is by induction on k.
item.dc:creator: Jicheng Ma

item.title: Kronecker Products, Polarity Quotients and Large Graph Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2608.27253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a structural compatibility between the Kronecker product of bipartite graphs that admit polarity and their polarity quotients, and provide a sharp upper bound on the diameter of these graphs. We use these properties to construct new families of graphs, all of which have orders that asymptotically approach the Moore bound. We show that the bipartite compatibility graphs have a natural polarity, and that the corresponding polarity quotients comprise a new family of graphs of any even diameter $2k$ with degree $(q+1)^k$ for any prime power $q$, much smaller than those of other known families of that diameter and field order $q$. These families generalize the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi-Brown polarity graphs. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of any even diameter for every pair of prime powers $q,r$. Certain generalized polygons are known to admit polarity with polarity quotients approaching the Moore bound asymptotically. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of diameters $2$, $3$ and $5$, including a diameter-$3$ degree-$18$ graph of order larger than any previously known for that degree and diameter.
item.dc:creator: Kelly Isham, Kartik Lakhotia, Laura Monroe, Fabrizio Petrini

item.title: Connected irregular cospectral graphs with distinct Lov\'{a}sz numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.10884v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every integer $n \geq 11$, we construct connected, irregular, nonisomorphic graphs on $n$ vertices with equal adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel spectra and equal independence, clique, chromatic, complement chromatic, and maximum-cut numbers, but distinct Lov\'{a}sz $\vartheta$-numbers. We join each graph in a fixed cospectral, nonisomorphic regular pair on ten vertices, due to van Dam and Haemers (2003), with $K_{n-10}$. We prove that these joins preserve equality of the five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants, and leave the respective Lov\'{a}sz numbers unchanged. We derive exact expressions for these numbers and prove that they are distinct. We also determine the cardinality-constrained maximum-cut profiles of both base graphs and their complements, yielding exact formulas and equality of maximum-cut numbers for the joins of either the base graphs or their complements with $K_{n-10}$. For $n=10$, we present a regular pair satisfying all stated properties except irregularity, followed by a connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair satisfying all properties. An exhaustive computer search finds no connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair on at most nine vertices sharing the first four spectra and all stated integer-valued invariants. Thus, ten is the smallest possible order, and such pairs exist for every $n \geq 10$. This extends and strengthens Sason's (2024) result for \emph{even} $n \geq 14$, which used the neighbors splitting join operation and did not address Seidel matrices, complement chromatic numbers, or maximum-cut numbers of the graphs or joins of their complements. Thus, the Lov\'{a}sz number efficiently certifies nonisomorphism even when all five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants coincide.
item.dc:creator: Igal Sason

item.title: Simple Cayley permutations
item.description: arXiv:2609.19078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a notion of simplicity for Cayley permutations that is compatible with inflation and agrees, under a natural relational encoding, with indecomposability in the sense of Schmerl and Trotter. We establish a substitution decomposition analogous to that of permutations, in which the components are modules of the associated relational structure. We use it to enumerate simple Cayley permutations as well as simple restricted growth functions.
item.dc:creator: Giulio Cerbai, Anders Claesson

item.title: Erd\H{o}s-S\'{o}s via random cyclic orderings
item.description: arXiv:2609.21159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a simplified proof of the Erd\H{o}s-S\'os conjecture on trees in graphs, which is based on its recent resolution by GPT-6 Astra. At the same time, we also give another proof of the corresponding conjecture for antidirected trees in digraphs, posed by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed, and Thomass\'e, and we simplify recent proofs of Kalai's conjecture for tight trees in hypergraphs. Our proof uses the language of random cyclic orderings in order to take advantage of symmetries that were obscured in the original argument, and we hope that the reader will find it intuitive. We also characterize the extremal examples for Kalai's conjecture, and we generalize it to the setting of so-called fully directed $r$-uniform hypergraphs, whose edges are ordered $r$-tuples.
item.dc:creator: Bryce Frederickson

item.title: Chv\'atal's conjecture: a proof from The Book
item.description: arXiv:2609.28404v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chv\'atal conjectured that every downset has a maximum-size intersecting family which is a star, that is, consists of all members of the downset containing a fixed element. Recently, Chang, Liu and Liu gave a proof of this conjecture, which follows as a corollary of more general results such as Kleitman's conjecture and a version of Kahn's conjecture (which they also prove). We give a short, direct (spectral) proof of Chv\'atal's conjecture, and a proof of Kleitman's conjecture along the same lines. We also prove a strengthening of Chv\'atal's conjecture concerning the projection packing number. Finally, we propose two spectral Chv\'atal conjectures which are motivated by extensive numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: David Ellis, Yuval Filmus, Ehud Friedgut
