item.title: Proper circular arc graphs are $e$-positive
item.description: arXiv:2609.33124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an $e$-positive formula for the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs solving the $q=1$ case of a conjecture of Ellzey and of Alexandersson and Panova. In doing so, we provide a new proof of the $e$-positivity of unit interval graphs, which alongside Guay-Paquet's reduction gives a new proof of the Stanley--Stembridge conjecture. We define color matrices, which count proper colorings, and tableau matrices, whose entries are nonnegative rational numbers and ratios of elementary symmetric functions. We prove the two matrices are related by a single family of change of basis matrices, which become invertible after restricting to finitely many colors, and we show the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs comes from taking the trace of these matrices. Using Hikita's tableaux, this gives an explicit formula for the chromatic symmetric function of a proper circular arc graph as a weighted sum over tableaux whose first and last $k$ vertices lie in the same columns.
item.dc:creator: Aarush Vailaya

item.title: On the maximum degree and order of $K_t$-minor-free graphs with positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.08706v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent results on the order of connected graphs with positive Lin--Lu--Yau Ricci curvature under forbidden minor or forbidden subgraph conditions and minimum degree assumptions, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge 5$, every locally finite graph $G$ with no $K_t$ minor, minimum degree at least $t-1$ and positive Lin--Lu--Yau Ricci curvature on every edge satisfies \[ \Delta(G)=O(t^5\log^{3/2}t). \] The minimum degree condition $t-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $G$ is connected, then $G$ is finite and \[|V(G)|<2t\Delta(G)^6=O(t^{31}\log^9 t). \]
item.dc:creator: Zi-Xia Song

item.title: Tur\'an densities of hypergraph augmentations
item.description: arXiv:2610.11757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $t$-graph $F$ and an integer $r\ge t$, the \emph{$r$-augmentation} $F(r)$ is the $r$-graph obtained by adding the same set of $r-t$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. We investigate the behaviour of the \emph{Tur\'an density $\pi(F(r))$}, which is the asymptotically maximum edge density of a large $F(r)$-free $r$-graph, as a function of $r\to\infty$. Let $H_k^r$ be the $r$-augmentation of the complete $(k-1)$-graph on $k$ vertices; equivalently, $H_k^r$ is the (unique up to isomorphism) $r$-graph with $r+1$ vertices and $k$ edges. This paper determines the Tur\'an density of each $r$-graph $H_k^r$ within a constant factor and estimates the lower bounds on $\pi(H_k^r)$ coming from the circular construction of Sidorenko. In particular, it is shown that if $k/\log r\to\infty$ then $\pi(H_k^r)=(1+o(1))k/r$. Also, we consider augmentations of graphs (that is, the case $t=2$) and prove that $\pi(F(r))\ge(\log r)^{-1-o(1)}/r$ for every 3-chromatic graph $F$, which comes close to the known upper bound $1/r$. Note that, for all other graphs $F$, the function $\pi(F(r))$ is known to be either identically 0 or uniformly bounded away from 0.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Pikhurko, Jiabao Yang, Xiutao Zhu

item.title: Clean handshake sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.17602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.
item.dc:creator: John Byrne, Colby Sherwood, Brian Wilmarth

item.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21217v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yohji Akama

item.title: On decomposition thresholds for odd cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of a fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. This settles the remaining cases $\ell=5,7,\ldots,71$ and completes the determination of the thresholds for all odd cycles. Our main ingredient is a sharp fractional decomposition theorem for weighted triangles: for every real $a\ge 1$,every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge \left(\frac12+\frac{1}{2(a+1)}\right)n$ admits a fractional decomposition into triangles with edge weights $a,1,1$.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Hou, Caiyun Hu, Hezhi Wang

item.title: The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27510v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $\chi_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ \chi_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Craig Timmons

item.title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.28030v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $\rho(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $\rho(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Bla\v{z}ej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $\rho(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $\Theta(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Sabaei, Fatemeh Emami, Yasmin Tousinejad

item.title: The Recursive Behavior of the Number of Irreducible Factors of Certain Rational Transformations over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2310.01872v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Constructing irreducible polynomials over finite fields via rational transformations is an active field of study. In this paper, we show that the method can be used for more than that. By considering normalized rational functions $Q$ that generate an invariant subfield $\mathbb{F}_q(x)^G$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(x)$, for a subgroup $G\le Aut(\mathbb{F}_q(x)/\mathbb{F}_q)$, and exploiting the factorization pattern of their rational transformations, we are able to prove that the sets arising from considering whether the rational transformation $f^Q$ has exactly $deg(Q)$ irreducible factors of the same degree as $f$, or an irreducible factor of higher degree, admit a recursive behavior, i.e. their numbers satisfy a recursive equation. These sets occasionally can be described in terms of arithmetical properties the roots of the irreducible polynomials satisfy, e.g. their roots satisfy certain trace or power/non-power conditions. These can often be translated to properties of their minimal polynomials. With that, we prove a new theorem about the number of certain irreducible factors of a class of linearized polynomials, which gives a new context to a recent paper by Granger.
item.dc:creator: Max Schulz

item.title: NP-Completeness and ETH-Based Additive Inapproximability of Deterministic Communication Complexity via Relaxed Interlacing
item.description: arXiv:2508.05597v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How difficult is it to find an efficient communication protocol when the entire truth table of the function is given? We give a unified interlacing proof of NP-completeness for exact optimisation and of hardness of approximation. Assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis, there is a computable, nondecreasing additive error allowance tending to infinity for which approximation is impossible in polynomial time. The proof uses interlacing, which asks the players to solve one problem selected by Alice from a collection of inputs held by Bob. For suitable matrices, a short protocol must reveal enough of Alice's selection to encode a solution to a combinatorial problem. This produces a one-bit communication gap in a polynomial-size matrix and proves exact hardness. Repeating the construction is harder: earlier messages can remove the inputs on which a later lower bound depends. Restriction bounds that survive the construction make the one-bit gain repeatable. A smaller, balanced family of interlaced columns controls the truth-table size. For every fixed number of applications, the construction takes subexponential time in the source length. This rules out every fixed additive error under ETH. A general computability argument then yields the stated unbounded allowance.
item.dc:creator: Serge Gaspers, Tao Zixu He, Simon Mackenzie

item.title: On generalized covering radii of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes
item.description: arXiv:2603.21068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The generalized covering radii (GCR) of linear codes are a fundamental higher-dimensional extension of the classical covering radius. While the second and third GCR of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes, $\text{BCH}(2,m)$, were recently determined, their proofs relied on highly complex combinatorial arguments, and the behavior of the GCR hierarchy for larger orders $k$ has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Generalized Supercode Lemma, which lower-bounds the GCR of a code using the generalized Hamming weights of an appropriate supercode. Applying this lemma, we significantly streamline and simplify the proofs for the known lower bounds of $\rho_2(\text{BCH}(2,m))$ and $\rho_3(\text{BCH}(2,m))$, and we establish a new lower bound for $\rho_4(\text{BCH}(2,m))$. Furthermore, by combining combinatorial arguments with Weil-type exponential sum estimates, we investigate the GCR hierarchy for general $k$, proving that $2k \le \rho_k(\text{BCH}(2,m)) \le 2k+1$ whenever $m$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$.
item.dc:creator: Maosheng Xiong, Chi Hoi Yip

item.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.25540v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.
item.dc:creator: Pimeng Dai, Li Yu

item.title: Caps and LCD Codes with Large Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2604.03734v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a connection between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and caps in projective space. Using this framework and the structure theory of maximal binary caps, we derive nonexistence theorems for binary LCD codes with minimum distance at least $4$, providing computation-free proofs that were previously obtained only through exhaustive search. As an application, we completely determine the optimal minimum distances for codimensions $7$ and $8$ for the first time. The framework applies to ternary LCD codes and quaternary Hermitian LCD codes, where it reduces the problem to the structure of large caps. Using known results on large caps, we determine the optimal minimum distances of ternary LCD codes of codimension $6$ for all lengths, and we explain why the phenomena behind the binary nonexistence theorems, such as the dependence on the parity of the length, have no counterpart for these codes.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka, Yuhi Kamio

item.title: On $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient ratios for complex parameters
item.description: arXiv:2607.08163v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove local asymptotics for near-central complex $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient modulus ratios allowing an imaginary parameter perturbation of order $n^{-3/4}$ at a $\sqrt{n}$ length scale from the centre. Moreover, we obtain ratio asymptotics for a smaller imaginary perturbation of order $n^{-5/4}$ at the length scale $n^{3/4}$. These results were obtained by reducing the two-parameter coefficients to just one parameter, giving a branch-free logarithmic representation of the second-order ratio and, hence, uniform complex curvature asymptotics for near-central ratios.
item.dc:creator: Per {\AA}hag, Rafa{\l} Czy\.z, Per-H{\aa}kan Lundow

item.title: Quartic Fourier-Laplace limits for $(p,q)$-Rogers-Szeg\H{o} polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.09150v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove asymptotic formulae for $(p,q)$-Rogers--Szeg\H{o} polynomials with positive real parameters when the leading quadratic term in the logarithmic expansion about the middle coefficient vanishes. For coefficient indices whose distance from $n/2$ is of order $n^{3/4}$, the coefficient ratios have a quadratic--quartic exponential limit. A uniform bound valid for all indices allows the ratios to be summed and gives locally uniform convergence of the centred and normalised generating polynomials to a Fourier--Laplace integral. We also obtain an asymptotic formula for the sum of the coefficients, convergence of all rescaled moments, weak convergence of the normalised coefficient measures, and convergence with multiplicity of the zeros near $w=1$ for which $n^{3/4}\log w$ remains bounded.
item.dc:creator: Per {\AA}hag, Rafa{\l} Czy\.z, Per-H{\aa}kan Lundow

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$, introduced by Kamae, Widmer and Zamboni, of infinite words $\alpha \in \mathbb{A}^{\mathbb{N}_{0}}$ over finite alphabets $\mathbb{A}$. For recurrent aperiodic words, we determine a lower bound and prove its sharpness. We further give a structural characterization of the words with minimal Abelian maximal pattern complexity. In the general case, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every $k.$ For aperiodic words over $\ell \geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq (\ell -1)(k-\ell +2)$, for all $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell -1)k}+O_{\ell }(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, at every $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset \mathbb{N}_{0}$ for which the bipartite graph on two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_{0}$, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$, is a forest.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: On Densities in the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer Distance Problems over the Integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.10665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the classical Erd\H{o}s and Falconer distance problems and Magyar's work on distance sets in $\mathbb Z^d$, we study discrete analogues of the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer unpinned and pinned distance problems over the integers. We ask how the discrete Hausdorff dimension of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ influences the size of its squared-distance sets, measured by generalized upper natural density and upper discrete mass dimension. We propose conjectures for both problems and prove the unpinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2,3$ and the pinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2$. For the unpinned problem in higher dimensions, we obtain explicit lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets using elementary integer sphere counting, results on the Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem, and $\ell^p$-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. For the pinned problem, we obtain lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets for some or every pin. We also establish more general results involving upper discrete mass dimension, upper discrete Banach dimension, and affine dimension, including bounds on the affine dimension of the exceptional set of pins. We construct examples showing that both conjectures are sharp in low dimensions. Further examples demonstrate how the distinctions among discrete Hausdorff dimension, upper discrete mass dimension, and upper discrete Banach dimension lead to different phenomena in the unpinned and pinned distance problems, including limitations on the nontrivial upper bounds these dimensions can provide for the dimensions of distance sets.
item.dc:creator: Eyvindur Ari Palsson, Jian-An Wang

item.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.11785v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bieliavsky, Victor Gayral, Sergey Neshveyev, Lars Tuset

item.title: Almost every Boolean function has central threshold degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.15057v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The polynomial threshold degree (or threshold degree) of a Boolean function is the least degree of a real polynomial whose sign represents it. We prove that almost every Boolean function has polynomial threshold degree among the central one or two integers. More precisely, a uniformly chosen Boolean function on $n$ variables has threshold degree either $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/2\rceil$, except with probability at most $\exp(-c2^{n/2}/n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The paper proves a 1991 conjecture of Aspnes, Beigel, Furst and Rudich. It also proves a 1991 conjecture of Wang and Williams for even $n$ and its main concentration assertion for odd $n$. A parity example gives a lower bound on the exceptional probability whose exponent differs from ours by a factor of order $n$. The proof relates polynomial sign representation to recovery of Reed--Muller codes from random erasures, and combines sharp-threshold estimates with bounds on generalized Hamming weights and minimum distance.
item.dc:creator: Martin Anthony
